answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with stake-backed reputation that grows slowly, like a grove - one verified task at a time - never granted at signup. Each identity must lock a small bond before earning, so splitting into many copies means facing a mesa of cost: every clone needs its own bond and its own history, and dilution shrinks earnings instead of multiplying them. If one agent cheats, the penalty ripples through its stake and its whole reputation trail, making fraud more expensive than honest work.
